newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CK Infra takes stake in China roads.
newsitem.headline: CK Infra takes stake in China roads.

text.p: Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) said on Thursday it has agreed to pay 383 million yuan for a 66 percent stake in two sections of China's National Highway 107 which links the north and the south.

CKI signed a contract with Chinese authorities on Wednesday to acquire the interest in 113 km of highway in Zhumadian in central China's Henan province, senior manager in planning and investment Tony Tsoi told Reuters.
CKI will be able to hold the stake for 27 years, he said.
The road sections are already in operation and ready to generate profit for the company, CKI said in a statement.
National Highway 107 is a main artery connecting northern and southern China and an essential part of the Chinese highway network, it said.
"CKI is currently in negotiations for a number of additional infrastructure projects in Henan province," managing director H.L. Kam said in the statement.
The company now has a total of 712 km of roads in its China transportation investment portfolio, representing a total road and bridge investment of about HK$5.8 billion.
